_doc: Modifier vocabulary. 'triggers' are matched (after normalisation) anywhere outside a recognised style phrase. 'effect' is shown verbatim to Claude in the routing brief: it must be an actionable art-direction instruction that ADJUSTS the base style without abandoning its signature rules. Add entries freely.

modifiers.effect: Push the palette 25-35% darker: deepen the base, lower midtone lightness, shift hues slightly cooler, concentrate light into one or two motivated sources, add a soft vignette. Keep the style's own line/shape rules unchanged.
Lift the palette 20-30%: light base, reduce shadow density, widen highlights, use warmer or cleaner hues. Keep contrast sufficient for the subject to stay legible.
Cut saturation ~35-50%, narrow contrast slightly, prefer greyed and chalky versions of the style's hues. (For 'pastel', raise lightness too.)
Raise saturation and hue separation: purer accents, fewer greys, complementary pairs next to each other. Keep one dominant colour so it does not turn into confetti.

Cut detail ~60%: keep only silhouette-defining shapes, 3-4 colours, generous negative space (>=40% of canvas). Preserve ONE signature technique of the base style (e.g. a single neon edge, one halftone area) so it is still recognisably that style.
Raise detail: add secondary forms, layered depth, pattern fills, small props and edge detail. Keep a clear focal point and a strong silhouette so the added detail does not flatten the hierarchy.

Use natural proportions and anatomy, motivated single-source lighting with cast shadows, subtle tonal modelling and material cues while keeping the base style's rendering vocabulary (its inks, edges, textures). Never embed a raster; build the realism from layered gradients and many small shapes.
Exaggerate proportions and shapes, simplify anatomy into strong geometric primitives, push silhouette and gesture.
Large head, small body, big low-set eyes, rounded terminals, soft palette, small blush accents, no sharp corners.
Bouncy asymmetry, slightly off-grid rotations, saturated friendly accents, small decorative confetti/sparkle elements, round terminals.
Restrained palette, symmetrical or grid-locked layout, consistent stroke weight, no novelty decoration, clean typography.
Dark or ivory base, restrained metallic accents (gradient gold/champagne), hairline strokes, generous margins, fine symmetrical ornament.
Add wear: irregular edges (feTurbulence/feDisplacementMap on ONE group, or hand-nudged points), speckle/scratch layers at low opacity, uneven ink density, colour registration offsets.
Remove texture and imperfections; exact geometry, consistent stroke weights, aligned edges, tidy spacing.
Shift palette toward amber/coral/rust; warm lights vs cool-tinted shadows; keep neutrals slightly creamy.
Shift palette toward teal/blue/violet; cool lights vs slightly warm accent for contrast.

Keep the base style's forms, line and ornament exactly, but replace its historical palette with a contemporary one: clean off-white or deep ink base, 1-2 saturated accents (e.g. electric blue, coral, mint), softened neutrals. No sepia/parchment tones.
Warm off-white paper base, desaturated primaries, ink-black or dark brown key colour, slight yellowing toward edges.
Add a neon accent set (hot magenta, cyan, electric violet, acid yellow) on a dark ground; use controlled glow on 2-4 hero edges only.
Restrict to one hue (or two inks for duotone) plus paper; express form purely through value, line and pattern.
Compress midtones, separate values hard, use the darkest dark and lightest light in the palette, keep shapes graphic.
Rounder corners, lower contrast edges, gradients instead of hard shadows, atmospheric haze layers at low opacity.
Increase stroke weight ~50-100%, simplify inner detail, enlarge shapes, tighten composition.
Reduce stroke to hairline (about 1/3 of the base weight), remove or lighten fills, rely on line hierarchy and negative space.
Build one half and mirror it with <use transform="matrix(-1 0 0 1 W 0)"> around the axis; align all key features to the axis.
Diagonal composition, foreshortened forms, speed lines or motion smear, strong value contrast at the focal point.
Horizontal structure, generous negative space, low contrast, single soft focal point, slow curves.
Cold sickly palette with one warm point of light, elongated or distorted proportions, deep vignette, fog layers, off-balance framing.
Add HUD-like linework, thin technical strokes, glowing accent edges, grid or circuit motifs, cool-biased palette.
Introduce controlled imperfection: slightly irregular line weight, wobble in paths (hand-nudged points), slight mis-registration between fill and outline.
Construct the subject from a small set of primitives (circles, triangles, arcs) on a hidden grid.
Omit the background rect entirely so the artwork sits on transparency; keep a soft shadow only if the style needs grounding.
Use a square viewBox (e.g. 0 0 1024 1024).
Use a wide viewBox (e.g. 0 0 1600 900); compose along the horizontal with the subject on a third.
Use a tall viewBox (e.g. 0 0 900 1400 or 0 0 900 1600); stack focal image, title and supporting text vertically.
